485	func (h *Handler) ServeHTTP(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, next caddyhttp.Handler) error {
486		repl := r.Context().Value(caddy.ReplacerCtxKey).(*caddy.Replacer)
487	
488		// prepare the request for proxying; this is needed only once
489		clonedReq, err := h.prepareRequest(r, repl)
490		if err != nil {
491			return caddyhttp.Error(http.StatusInternalServerError,
492				fmt.Errorf("preparing request for upstream round-trip: %v", err))
493		}
494	
495		// websocket over http2 or http3 if extended connect is enabled, assuming backend doesn't support this, the request will be modified to http1.1 upgrade
496		// Both use the same upgrade mechanism: server advertizes extended connect support, and client sends the pseudo header :protocol in a CONNECT request
497		// The quic-go http3 implementation also puts :protocol in r.Proto for CONNECT requests (quic-go/http3/headers.go@70-72,185,203)
498		// TODO: once we can reliably detect backend support this, it can be removed for those backends
499		if (r.ProtoMajor == 2 && r.Method == http.MethodConnect && r.Header.Get(":protocol") == "websocket") ||
500			(r.ProtoMajor == 3 && r.Method == http.MethodConnect && r.Proto == "websocket") {
501			clonedReq.Header.Del(":protocol")
502			// keep the body for later use. http1.1 upgrade uses http.NoBody
503			caddyhttp.SetVar(clonedReq.Context(), "extended_connect_websocket_body", clonedReq.Body)
504			clonedReq.Body = http.NoBody
505			clonedReq.Method = http.MethodGet
506			clonedReq.Header.Set("Upgrade", "websocket")
507			clonedReq.Header.Set("Connection", "Upgrade")
508			key := make([]byte, 16)
509			_, randErr := rand.Read(key)
510			if randErr != nil {
511				return randErr
512			}
513			clonedReq.Header["Sec-WebSocket-Key"] = []string{base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(key)}
514		}
515	
516		// we will need the original headers and Host value if
517		// header operations are configured; this is so that each
518		// retry can apply the modifications, because placeholders
519		// may be used which depend on the selected upstream for
520		// their values
521		reqHost := clonedReq.Host
522		reqHeader := clonedReq.Header
523	
524		// If the request contained a body, wrap it in io.NopCloser
525		// to prevent Go's transport from closing it on dial errors.
526		// cloneRequest does a shallow copy, so clonedReq.Body and
527		// r.Body share the same io.ReadCloser — a dial-failure Close()
528		// would kill the original body for all subsequent retry
529		// attempts or subsequent handlers. The real body is closed by
530		// the HTTP server when the handler returns.
531		//
532		// If the body was already fully buffered (via request_buffers),
533		// we also extract the buffer so the retry loop can replay it
534		// from the beginning on each attempt. (see #6259, #7546, #7713)
535		var bufferedReqBody *bytes.Buffer
536		if clonedReq.Body != nil {
537			if reqBodyBuf, ok := clonedReq.Body.(bodyReadCloser); ok && reqBodyBuf.body == nil && reqBodyBuf.buf != nil {
538				bufferedReqBody = reqBodyBuf.buf
539				reqBodyBuf.buf = nil
540				clonedReq.Body = io.NopCloser(bytes.NewReader(bufferedReqBody.Bytes()))
541				defer func() {
542					bufferedReqBody.Reset()
543					bufPool.Put(bufferedReqBody)
544				}()
545			} else {
546				clonedReq.Body = &bodyNopCloserIfNotRead{ReadCloser: clonedReq.Body}
547			}
548		}
549	
550		start := time.Now()
551		defer func() {
552			// total proxying duration, including time spent on LB and retries
553			repl.Set("http.reverse_proxy.duration", time.Since(start))
554			repl.Set("http.reverse_proxy.duration_ms", time.Since(start).Seconds()*1e3) // multiply seconds to preserve decimal (see #4666)
555		}()
556	
557		// in the proxy loop, each iteration is an attempt to proxy the request,
558		// and because we may retry some number of times, carry over the error
559		// from previous tries because of the nuances of load balancing & retries
560		//
561		// triedUpstreams tracks the upstreams that have already been selected for
562		// this request and failed before producing a final response. It is scoped
563		// to this single client request only: it ensures a retry lands on a
564		// different upstream (selection policies such as random or round_robin do
565		// not guarantee that on their own, and "first" would otherwise re-select
566		// the same first upstream forever), and never leaks state between
567		// requests.
568		var proxyErr error
569		var retries int
570		triedUpstreams := make(map[string]struct{})
571		for {
572			// if the request body was buffered (and only the entire body, hence no body
573			// set to read from after the buffer), make reading from the body idempotent
574			// and reusable, so if a backend partially or fully reads the body but then
575			// produces an error, the request can be repeated to the next backend with
576			// the full body (retries should only happen for idempotent requests) (see #6259)
577			if bufferedReqBody != nil {
578				clonedReq.Body = io.NopCloser(bytes.NewReader(bufferedReqBody.Bytes()))
579			}
580	
581			var done bool
582			done, proxyErr = h.proxyLoopIteration(clonedReq, r, w, proxyErr, start, retries, repl, reqHeader, reqHost, next, triedUpstreams)
583			if done {
584				break
585			}
586			if h.VerboseLogs {
587				var lbWait time.Duration
588				if h.LoadBalancing != nil {
589					lbWait = time.Duration(h.LoadBalancing.TryInterval)
590				}
591				if c := h.logger.Check(zapcore.DebugLevel, "retrying"); c != nil {
592					c.Write(zap.Error(proxyErr), zap.Duration("after", lbWait))
593				}
594			}
595			retries++
596		}
597	
598		// number of retries actually performed
599		repl.Set("http.reverse_proxy.retries", retries)
600	
601		if proxyErr != nil {
602			return statusError(proxyErr)
603		}
604	
605		return nil
606	}
607	
608	// proxyLoopIteration implements an iteration of the proxy loop. Despite the enormous amount of local state
609	// that has to be passed in, we brought this into its own method so that we could run defer more easily.
610	// It returns true when the loop is done and should break; false otherwise. The error value returned should
611	// be assigned to the proxyErr value for the next iteration of the loop (or the error handled after break).
612	func (h *Handler) proxyLoopIteration(r *http.Request, origReq *http.Request, w http.ResponseWriter, proxyErr error, start time.Time, retries int,
613		repl *caddy.Replacer, reqHeader http.Header, reqHost string, next caddyhttp.Handler, triedUpstreams map[string]struct{},
614	) (bool, error) {
615		// get the updated list of upstreams
616		upstreams := h.Upstreams
617		if h.DynamicUpstreams != nil {
618			if retries > 0 {
619				// after a failure (and thus during a retry), give dynamic upstream modules an opportunity
620				// to purge their relevant cache entries so we don't keep retrying bad upstreams
621				if cachingDynamicUpstreams, ok := h.DynamicUpstreams.(CachingUpstreamSource); ok {
622					if err := cachingDynamicUpstreams.ResetCache(r); err != nil {
623						if c := h.logger.Check(zapcore.ErrorLevel, "failed clearing dynamic upstream source's cache"); c != nil {
624							c.Write(zap.Error(err))
625						}
626					}
627				}
628			}
629			dUpstreams, err := h.DynamicUpstreams.GetUpstreams(r)
630			if err != nil {
631				if c := h.logger.Check(zapcore.ErrorLevel, "failed getting dynamic upstreams; falling back to static upstreams"); c != nil {
632					c.Write(zap.Error(err))
633				}
634			} else {
635				upstreams = dUpstreams
636				for _, dUp := range dUpstreams {
637					h.provisionUpstream(dUp, true)
638				}
639				if c := h.logger.Check(zapcore.DebugLevel, "provisioned dynamic upstreams"); c != nil {
640					c.Write(zap.Int("count", len(dUpstreams)))
641				}
642			}
643		}
644	
645		// choose an available upstream; upstreams already attempted for this
646		// request are excluded so that a retry is served by a different
647		// upstream, regardless of selection policy
648		upstream := h.selectUpstream(upstreams, r, w, repl, triedUpstreams)
649		if upstream == nil {
650			if proxyErr == nil {
651				proxyErr = caddyhttp.Error(http.StatusServiceUnavailable, errNoUpstream)
652			}
653			if !h.LoadBalancing.tryAgain(h.ctx, start, retries, proxyErr, r, h.logger) {
654				return true, proxyErr
655			}
656			return false, proxyErr
657		}
658	
659		// the dial address may vary per-request if placeholders are
660		// used, so perform those replacements here; the resulting
661		// DialInfo struct should have valid network address syntax
662		dialInfo, err := upstream.fillDialInfo(repl)
663		if err != nil {
664			return true, fmt.Errorf("making dial info: %v", err)
665		}
666	
667		if c := h.logger.Check(zapcore.DebugLevel, "selected upstream"); c != nil {
668			c.Write(
669				zap.String("dial", dialInfo.Address),
670				zap.Int("total_upstreams", len(upstreams)),
671			)
672		}
673	
674		// attach to the request information about how to dial the upstream;
675		// this is necessary because the information cannot be sufficiently
676		// or satisfactorily represented in a URL
677		caddyhttp.SetVar(r.Context(), dialInfoVarKey, dialInfo)
678	
679		// set placeholders with information about this upstream
680		repl.Set("http.reverse_proxy.upstream.address", dialInfo.String())
681		repl.Set("http.reverse_proxy.upstream.hostport", dialInfo.Address)
682		repl.Set("http.reverse_proxy.upstream.host", dialInfo.Host)
683		repl.Set("http.reverse_proxy.upstream.port", dialInfo.Port)
684		repl.Set("http.reverse_proxy.upstream.requests", upstream.Host.NumRequests())
685		repl.Set("http.reverse_proxy.upstream.max_requests", upstream.MaxRequests)
686		repl.Set("http.reverse_proxy.upstream.fails", upstream.Host.Fails())
687	
688		// mutate request headers according to this upstream;
689		// because we're in a retry loop, we have to copy headers
690		// (and the r.Host value) from the original so that each
691		// retry is identical to the first. If either transport or
692		// user ops exist, apply them in order (transport first,
693		// then user, so user's config wins).
694		var userOps *headers.HeaderOps
695		if h.Headers != nil {
696			userOps = h.Headers.Request
697		}
698		transportOps := h.transportHeaderOps
699		if transportOps != nil || userOps != nil {
700			r.Header = make(http.Header)
701			copyHeader(r.Header, reqHeader)
702			r.Host = reqHost
703			if transportOps != nil {
704				transportOps.ApplyToRequest(r)
705			}
706			if userOps != nil {
707				userOps.ApplyToRequest(r)
708			}
709		}
710	
711		// proxy the request to that upstream
712		proxyErr = h.reverseProxy(w, r, origReq, repl, dialInfo, next)
713		if proxyErr == nil || errors.Is(proxyErr, context.Canceled) {
714			// context.Canceled happens when the downstream client
715			// cancels the request, which is not our failure
716			return true, nil
717		}
718	
719		// if the roundtrip was successful, don't retry the request or
720		// ding the health status of the upstream (an error can still
721		// occur after the roundtrip if, for example, a response handler
722		// after the roundtrip returns an error)
723		if succ, ok := proxyErr.(roundtripSucceededError); ok {
724			return true, succ.error
725		}
726	
727		// remember this failure (if enabled); response-based retries
728		// are not counted as failures since the upstream did respond
729		// successfully - only the response content triggered a retry
730		if _, isRetryableResponse := proxyErr.(retryableResponseError); !isRetryableResponse {
731			h.countFailure(upstream)
732		}
733	
734		// exclude this upstream from any further attempt for the same
735		// client request, so a retry moves to a different upstream
736		// rather than being served by the one that just failed
737		triedUpstreams[dialInfo.Address] = struct{}{}
738	
739		// if we've tried long enough, break
740		if !h.LoadBalancing.tryAgain(h.ctx, start, retries, proxyErr, r, h.logger) {
741			return true, proxyErr
742		}
743	
744		return false, proxyErr
745	}
746	
747	// selectUpstream applies the configured selection policy to pool, preferring
748	// upstreams that have not already been attempted for the current request
749	// (keyed by their resolved dial address). This keeps retry semantics
750	// independent of the policy: for example, "first" would otherwise re-select
751	// the same first upstream on every attempt, and random or round_robin
752	// policies do not promise a different upstream either. The exclusion set is
753	// per-request and carries no health state, so it never affects subsequent
754	// client requests.
755	//
756	// If every available upstream has already been attempted, the unfiltered
757	// policy is used as a fallback; the retry limit (and/or try duration) remains
758	// responsible for deciding when to stop, preserving the previous behaviour
759	// for pools with a single upstream.
760	func (h *Handler) selectUpstream(pool UpstreamPool, r *http.Request, w http.ResponseWriter,
761		repl *caddy.Replacer, triedUpstreams map[string]struct{},
762	) *Upstream {
763		policy := h.LoadBalancing.SelectionPolicy
764		if len(triedUpstreams) == 0 {
765			return policy.Select(pool, r, w)
766		}
767		candidates := make(UpstreamPool, 0, len(pool))
768		for _, u := range pool {
769			// resolve the same dial address that proxyLoopIteration uses
770			// below; an unresolvable address is left in as a candidate so
771			// that its existing, terminal configuration error is surfaced
772			di, err := u.fillDialInfo(repl)
773			if err != nil {
774				candidates = append(candidates, u)
775				continue
776			}
777			if _, tried := triedUpstreams[di.Address]; !tried {
778				candidates = append(candidates, u)
779			}
780		}
781		if len(candidates) == 0 {
782			// all available upstreams were already attempted; fall back to
783			// the unfiltered pool and let the retry budget terminate the loop
784			candidates = pool
785		}
786		return policy.Select(candidates, r, w)
787	}
788	
789	// Mapping of the canonical form of the headers, to the RFC 6455 form,
790	// i.e. `WebSocket` with uppercase 'S'.
791	var websocketHeaderMapping = map[string]string{
792		"Sec-Websocket-Accept":     "Sec-WebSocket-Accept",
793		"Sec-Websocket-Extensions": "Sec-WebSocket-Extensions",
794		"Sec-Websocket-Key":        "Sec-WebSocket-Key",
795		"Sec-Websocket-Protocol":   "Sec-WebSocket-Protocol",
796		"Sec-Websocket-Version":    "Sec-WebSocket-Version",
797	}
798	
799	// normalizeWebsocketHeaders ensures we use the standard casing as per
800	// RFC 6455, i.e. `WebSocket` with uppercase 'S'. Most servers don't
801	// care about this difference (read headers case insensitively), but
802	// some do, so this maximizes compatibility with upstreams.
803	// See https://github.com/caddyserver/caddy/pull/6621
804	func normalizeWebsocketHeaders(header http.Header) {
805		for k, rk := range websocketHeaderMapping {
806			if v, ok := header[k]; ok {
807				delete(header, k)
808				header[rk] = v
809			}
810		}
811	}
812	
813	// prepareRequest clones req so that it can be safely modified without
814	// changing the original request or introducing data races. It then
815	// modifies it so that it is ready to be proxied, except for directing
816	// to a specific upstream. This method adjusts headers and other relevant
817	// properties of the cloned request and should be done just once (before
818	// proxying) regardless of proxy retries. This assumes that no mutations
819	// of the cloned request are performed by h during or after proxying.
820	func (h Handler) prepareRequest(req *http.Request, repl *caddy.Replacer) (*http.Request, error) {
821		req = cloneRequest(req)
822	
823		// if enabled, perform rewrites on the cloned request; if
824		// the method is GET or HEAD, prevent the request body
825		// from being copied to the upstream
826		if h.Rewrite != nil {
827			changed := h.Rewrite.Rewrite(req, repl)
828			if changed && (h.Rewrite.Method == "GET" || h.Rewrite.Method == "HEAD") {
829				req.ContentLength = 0
830				req.Body = nil
831			}
832		}
833	
834		// if enabled, buffer client request; this should only be
835		// enabled if the upstream requires it and does not work
836		// with "slow clients" (gunicorn, etc.) - this obviously
837		// has a perf overhead and makes the proxy at risk of
838		// exhausting memory and more susceptible to slowloris
839		// attacks, so it is strongly recommended to only use this
840		// feature if absolutely required, if read timeouts are
841		// set, and if body size is limited
842		if h.RequestBuffers != 0 && req.Body != nil {
843			var readBytes int64
844			req.Body, readBytes = h.bufferedBody(req.Body, h.RequestBuffers)
845			// set Content-Length when body is fully buffered
846			if b, ok := req.Body.(bodyReadCloser); ok && b.body == nil {
847				req.ContentLength = readBytes
848				req.Header.Set("Content-Length", strconv.FormatInt(req.ContentLength, 10))
849			}
850		}
851	
852		if req.ContentLength == 0 {
853			req.Body = nil // Issue golang/go#16036: nil Body for http.Transport retries
854		}
855	
856		req.Close = false
857	
858		// if User-Agent is not set by client, then explicitly
859		// disable it so it's not set to default value by std lib
860		if _, ok := req.Header["User-Agent"]; !ok {
861			req.Header.Set("User-Agent", "")
862		}
863	
864		// Indicate if request has been conveyed in early data.
865		// RFC 8470: "An intermediary that forwards a request prior to the
866		// completion of the TLS handshake with its client MUST send it with
867		// the Early-Data header field set to “1” (i.e., it adds it if not
868		// present in the request). An intermediary MUST use the Early-Data
869		// header field if the request might have been subject to a replay and
870		// might already have been forwarded by it or another instance
871		// (see Section 6.2)."
872		if req.TLS != nil && !req.TLS.HandshakeComplete {
873			req.Header.Set("Early-Data", "1")
874		}
875	
876		reqUpgradeType := upgradeType(req.Header)
877		removeConnectionHeaders(req.Header)
878	
879		// Remove hop-by-hop headers to the backend. Especially
880		// important is "Connection" because we want a persistent
881		// connection, regardless of what the client sent to us.
882		// Issue golang/go#46313: don't skip if field is empty.
883		for _, h := range hopHeaders {
884			// Issue golang/go#21096: tell backend applications that care about trailer support
885			// that we support trailers. (We do, but we don't go out of our way to
886			// advertise that unless the incoming client request thought it was worth
887			// mentioning.)
888			if h == "Te" && httpguts.HeaderValuesContainsToken(req.Header["Te"], "trailers") {
889				req.Header.Set("Te", "trailers")
890				continue
891			}
892			req.Header.Del(h)
893		}
894	
895		// After stripping all the hop-by-hop connection headers above, add back any
896		// necessary for protocol upgrades, such as for websockets.
897		if reqUpgradeType != "" {
898			req.Header.Set("Connection", "Upgrade")
899			req.Header.Set("Upgrade", reqUpgradeType)
900			normalizeWebsocketHeaders(req.Header)
901		}
902	
903		// Set up the PROXY protocol info
904		address := caddyhttp.GetVar(req.Context(), caddyhttp.ClientIPVarKey).(string)
905		addrPort, err := netip.ParseAddrPort(address)
906		if err != nil {
907			// OK; probably didn't have a port
908			addr, err := netip.ParseAddr(address)
909			if err != nil {
910				// Doesn't seem like a valid ip address at all
911			} else {
912				// Ok, only the port was missing
913				addrPort = netip.AddrPortFrom(addr, 0)
914			}
915		}
916		proxyProtocolInfo := ProxyProtocolInfo{AddrPort: addrPort}
917		caddyhttp.SetVar(req.Context(), proxyProtocolInfoVarKey, proxyProtocolInfo)
918	
919		// some of the outbound requests require h1 (e.g. websocket)
920		// https://github.com/golang/go/blob/4837fbe4145cd47b43eed66fee9eed9c2b988316/src/net/http/request.go#L1579
921		if isWebsocket(req) {
922			caddyhttp.SetVar(req.Context(), tlsH1OnlyVarKey, true)
923		}
924	
925		// Add the supported X-Forwarded-* headers
926		err = h.addForwardedHeaders(req)
927		if err != nil {
928			return nil, err
929		}
930	
931		// Via header(s)
932		req.Header.Add("Via", fmt.Sprintf("%d.%d Caddy", req.ProtoMajor, req.ProtoMinor))
933	
934		return req, nil
935	}

937	// addForwardedHeaders adds the de-facto standard X-Forwarded-*
938	// headers to the request before it is sent upstream.
939	//
940	// These headers are security sensitive, so care is taken to only
941	// use existing values for these headers from the incoming request
942	// if the client IP is trusted (i.e. coming from a trusted proxy
943	// sitting in front of this server). If the request didn't have
944	// the headers at all, then they will be added with the values
945	// that we can glean from the request.
946	func (h Handler) addForwardedHeaders(req *http.Request) error {
947		// Check if the client is a trusted proxy
948		trusted := caddyhttp.GetVar(req.Context(), caddyhttp.TrustedProxyVarKey).(bool)
949	
950		var clientIP string
951	
952		if req.RemoteAddr == "@" {
953			// For Unix socket connections, RemoteAddr is "@" which cannot
954			// be parsed as host:port. If untrusted, strip forwarded headers
955			// for security. If trusted, there is no peer IP to append to
956			// X-Forwarded-For, so clientIP stays empty.
957			if !trusted {
958				req.Header.Del("X-Forwarded-For")
959				req.Header.Del("X-Forwarded-Proto")
960				req.Header.Del("X-Forwarded-Host")
961				return nil
962			}
963		} else {
964			// Parse the remote IP, ignore the error as non-fatal,
965			// but the remote IP is required to continue, so we
966			// just return early. This should probably never happen
967			// though, unless some other module manipulated the request's
968			// remote address and used an invalid value.
969			var err error
970			clientIP, _, err = net.SplitHostPort(req.RemoteAddr)
971			if err != nil {
972				// Remove the `X-Forwarded-*` headers to avoid upstreams
973				// potentially trusting a header that came from the client
974				req.Header.Del("X-Forwarded-For")
975				req.Header.Del("X-Forwarded-Proto")
976				req.Header.Del("X-Forwarded-Host")
977				return nil
978			}
979	
980			// Client IP may contain a zone if IPv6, so we need
981			// to pull that out before parsing the IP
982			clientIP, _, _ = strings.Cut(clientIP, "%")
983			ipAddr, err := netip.ParseAddr(clientIP)
984	
985			// If ParseAddr fails (e.g. non-IP network like SCION), we cannot check
986			// if it is a trusted proxy by IP range. In this case, we ignore the
987			// error and treat the connection as untrusted (or retain existing status).
988			if err == nil {
989				for _, ipRange := range h.trustedProxies {
990					if ipRange.Contains(ipAddr) {
991						trusted = true
992						break
993					}
994				}
995			}
996		}
997	
998		// If we aren't the first proxy, and the proxy is trusted,
999		// retain prior X-Forwarded-For information as a comma+space
1000		// separated list and fold multiple headers into one.
1001		prior, ok, omit := allHeaderValues(req.Header, "X-Forwarded-For")
1002		if !omit {
1003			if trusted && ok && prior != "" {
1004				if clientIP != "" {
1005					req.Header.Set("X-Forwarded-For", prior+", "+clientIP)
1006				} else {
1007					req.Header.Set("X-Forwarded-For", prior)
1008				}
1009			} else if clientIP != "" {
1010				req.Header.Set("X-Forwarded-For", clientIP)
1011			}
1012		}
1013	
1014		// Set X-Forwarded-Proto; many backend apps expect this,
1015		// so that they can properly craft URLs with the right
1016		// scheme to match the original request
1017		proto := "https"
1018		if req.TLS == nil {
1019			proto = "http"
1020		}
1021		prior, ok, omit = lastHeaderValue(req.Header, "X-Forwarded-Proto")
1022		if trusted && ok && prior != "" {
1023			proto = prior
1024		}
1025		if !omit {
1026			req.Header.Set("X-Forwarded-Proto", proto)
1027		}
1028	
1029		// Set X-Forwarded-Host; often this is redundant because
1030		// we pass through the request Host as-is, but in situations
1031		// where we proxy over HTTPS, the user may need to override
1032		// Host themselves, so it's helpful to send the original too.
1033		host := req.Host
1034		prior, ok, omit = lastHeaderValue(req.Header, "X-Forwarded-Host")
1035		if trusted && ok && prior != "" {
1036			host = prior
1037		}
1038		if !omit {
1039			req.Header.Set("X-Forwarded-Host", host)
1040		}
1041	
1042		return nil
1043	}

1045	// reverseProxy performs a round-trip to the given backend and processes the response with the client.
1046	// (This method is mostly the beginning of what was borrowed from the net/http/httputil package in the
1047	// Go standard library which was used as the foundation.)
1048	func (h *Handler) reverseProxy(rw http.ResponseWriter, req *http.Request, origReq *http.Request, repl *caddy.Replacer, di DialInfo, next caddyhttp.Handler) error {
1049		_ = di.Upstream.Host.countRequest(1)
1050	
1051		// Increment the in-flight request count
1052		incInFlightRequest(di.Address)
1053	
1054		//nolint:errcheck
1055		defer func() {
1056			di.Upstream.Host.countRequest(-1)
1057			// Decrement the in-flight request count
1058			decInFlightRequest(di.Address)
1059		}()
1060	
1061		// point the request to this upstream
1062		h.directRequest(req, di)
1063	
1064		server := req.Context().Value(caddyhttp.ServerCtxKey).(*caddyhttp.Server)
1065		shouldLogCredentials := server.Logs != nil && server.Logs.ShouldLogCredentials
1066	
1067		// Forward 1xx status codes, backported from https://github.com/golang/go/pull/53164
1068		var (
1069			roundTripMutex sync.Mutex
1070			roundTripDone  bool
1071		)
1072		trace := &httptrace.ClientTrace{
1073			Got1xxResponse: func(code int, header textproto.MIMEHeader) error {
1074				roundTripMutex.Lock()
1075				defer roundTripMutex.Unlock()
1076				if roundTripDone {
1077					// If RoundTrip has returned, don't try to further modify
1078					// the ResponseWriter's header map.
1079					return nil
1080				}
1081				h := rw.Header()
1082				copyHeader(h, http.Header(header))
1083				rw.WriteHeader(code)
1084	
1085				// Clear headers coming from the backend
1086				// (it's not automatically done by ResponseWriter.WriteHeader() for 1xx responses)
1087				clear(h)
1088	
1089				return nil
1090			},
1091		}
1092		req = req.WithContext(httptrace.WithClientTrace(req.Context(), trace))
1093	
1094		// do the round-trip
1095		start := time.Now()
1096		res, err := h.Transport.RoundTrip(req)
1097		duration := time.Since(start)
1098	
1099		// record that the round trip is done for the 1xx response handler
1100		roundTripMutex.Lock()
1101		roundTripDone = true
1102		roundTripMutex.Unlock()
1103	
1104		// emit debug log with values we know are safe,
1105		// or if there is no error, emit fuller log entry
1106		logger := h.logger.With(
1107			zap.String("upstream", di.Upstream.String()),
1108			zap.Duration("duration", duration),
1109			zap.Object("request", caddyhttp.LoggableHTTPRequest{
1110				Request:              req,
1111				ShouldLogCredentials: shouldLogCredentials,
1112			}),
1113		)
1114	
1115		const logMessage = "upstream roundtrip"
1116	
1117		if err != nil {
1118			if c := logger.Check(zapcore.DebugLevel, logMessage); c != nil {
1119				c.Write(zap.Error(err))
1120			}
1121			return err
1122		}
1123		if c := logger.Check(zapcore.DebugLevel, logMessage); c != nil {
1124			c.Write(
1125				zap.Object("headers", caddyhttp.LoggableHTTPHeader{
1126					Header:               res.Header,
1127					ShouldLogCredentials: shouldLogCredentials,
1128				}),
1129				zap.Int("status", res.StatusCode),
1130			)
1131		}
1132	
1133		// duration until upstream wrote response headers (roundtrip duration)
1134		repl.Set("http.reverse_proxy.upstream.latency", duration)
1135		repl.Set("http.reverse_proxy.upstream.latency_ms", duration.Seconds()*1e3) // multiply seconds to preserve decimal (see #4666)
1136	
1137		// update circuit breaker on current conditions
1138		if di.Upstream.cb != nil {
1139			di.Upstream.cb.RecordMetric(res.StatusCode, duration)
1140		}
1141	
1142		// perform passive health checks (if enabled)
1143		if h.HealthChecks != nil && h.HealthChecks.Passive != nil {
1144			// strike if the status code matches one that is "bad"
1145			for _, badStatus := range h.HealthChecks.Passive.UnhealthyStatus {
1146				if caddyhttp.StatusCodeMatches(res.StatusCode, badStatus) {
1147					h.countFailure(di.Upstream)
1148				}
1149			}
1150	
1151			// strike if the roundtrip took too long
1152			if h.HealthChecks.Passive.UnhealthyLatency > 0 &&
1153				duration >= time.Duration(h.HealthChecks.Passive.UnhealthyLatency) {
1154				h.countFailure(di.Upstream)
1155			}
1156		}
1157	
1158		// if enabled, buffer the response body
1159		if h.ResponseBuffers != 0 {
1160			res.Body, _ = h.bufferedBody(res.Body, h.ResponseBuffers)
1161		}
1162	
1163		// set response placeholders so they can be used in retry match
1164		// expressions and handle_response routes; clear stale header
1165		// placeholders from a previous attempt first so they don't
1166		// leak into the next retry evaluation
1167		repl.DeleteByPrefix("http.reverse_proxy.header.")
1168		for field, value := range res.Header {
1169			repl.Set("http.reverse_proxy.header."+field, strings.Join(value, ","))
1170		}
1171		repl.Set("http.reverse_proxy.status_code", res.StatusCode)
1172		repl.Set("http.reverse_proxy.status_text", res.Status)
1173	
1174		// check if the response matches a retry match entry; if so,
1175		// close the body and return a retryable error so the request
1176		// is retried with the next upstream. Only evaluate matcher sets
1177		// that contain at least one expression matcher, since those are
1178		// the ones that can reference response data ({rp.status_code},
1179		// {rp.header.*}). Pure request-only matchers (method, path, etc.)
1180		// are skipped to avoid retrying every response that matches a
1181		// request condition
1182		if h.LoadBalancing != nil && len(h.LoadBalancing.RetryMatch) > 0 {
1183			for _, matcherSet := range h.LoadBalancing.RetryMatch {
1184				if !matcherSetHasExpressionMatcher(matcherSet) {
1185					continue
1186				}
1187				match, err := matcherSet.MatchWithError(req)
1188				if err != nil {
1189					h.logger.Error("error matching request for retry", zap.Error(err))
1190					break
1191				}
1192				if match {
1193					res.Body.Close()
1194					return retryableResponseError{
1195						error:      fmt.Errorf("upstream response matched retry_match (status %d)", res.StatusCode),
1196						statusCode: res.StatusCode,
1197					}
1198				}
1199			}
1200		}
1201	
1202		// see if any response handler is configured for this response from the backend
1203		for i, rh := range h.HandleResponse {
1204			if rh.Match != nil && !rh.Match.Match(res.StatusCode, res.Header) {
1205				continue
1206			}
1207	
1208			// if configured to only change the status code,
1209			// do that then continue regular proxy response
1210			if statusCodeStr := rh.StatusCode.String(); statusCodeStr != "" {
1211				statusCode, err := strconv.Atoi(repl.ReplaceAll(statusCodeStr, ""))
1212				if err != nil {
1213					return caddyhttp.Error(http.StatusInternalServerError, err)
1214				}
1215				if statusCode != 0 {
1216					res.StatusCode = statusCode
1217				}
1218				break
1219			}
1220	
1221			if c := logger.Check(zapcore.DebugLevel, "handling response"); c != nil {
1222				c.Write(zap.Int("handler", i))
1223			}
1224	
1225			// we make some data available via request context to child routes
1226			// so that they may inherit some options and functions from the
1227			// handler, and be able to copy the response.
1228			// we use the original request here, so that any routes from 'next'
1229			// see the original request rather than the proxy cloned request.
1230			hrc := &handleResponseContext{
1231				handler:  h,
1232				response: res,
1233				start:    start,
1234				logger:   logger,
1235			}
1236			ctx := origReq.Context()
1237			ctx = context.WithValue(ctx, proxyHandleResponseContextCtxKey, hrc)
1238	
1239			// pass the request through the response handler routes
1240			routeErr := rh.Routes.Compile(next).ServeHTTP(rw, origReq.WithContext(ctx))
1241	
1242			// close the response body afterwards, since we don't need it anymore;
1243			// either a route had 'copy_response' which already consumed the body,
1244			// or some other terminal handler ran which doesn't need the response
1245			// body after that point (e.g. 'file_server' for X-Accel-Redirect flow),
1246			// or we fell through to subsequent handlers past this proxy
1247			// (e.g. forward auth's 2xx response flow).
1248			if !hrc.isFinalized {
1249				res.Body.Close()
1250			}
1251	
1252			// wrap any route error in roundtripSucceededError so caller knows that
1253			// the roundtrip was successful and to not retry
1254			if routeErr != nil {
1255				return roundtripSucceededError{routeErr}
1256			}
1257	
1258			// we're done handling the response, and we don't want to
1259			// fall through to the default finalize/copy behaviour
1260			return nil
1261		}
1262	
1263		// copy the response body and headers back to the upstream client
1264		return h.finalizeResponse(rw, req, res, repl, start, logger)
1265	}

1267	// finalizeResponse prepares and copies the response.
1268	func (h *Handler) finalizeResponse(
1269		rw http.ResponseWriter,
1270		req *http.Request,
1271		res *http.Response,
1272		repl *caddy.Replacer,
1273		start time.Time,
1274		logger *zap.Logger,
1275	) error {
1276		// deal with 101 Switching Protocols responses: (WebSocket, h2c, etc)
1277		if res.StatusCode == http.StatusSwitchingProtocols {
1278			var wg sync.WaitGroup
1279			h.handleUpgradeResponse(logger, &wg, rw, req, res)
1280			wg.Wait()
1281			return nil
1282		}
1283	
1284		removeConnectionHeaders(res.Header)
1285	
1286		for _, h := range hopHeaders {
1287			res.Header.Del(h)
1288		}
1289	
1290		// delete our Server header and use Via instead (see #6275)
1291		rw.Header().Del("Server")
1292		var protoPrefix string
1293		if !strings.HasPrefix(strings.ToUpper(res.Proto), "HTTP/") {
1294			protoPrefix = res.Proto[:strings.Index(res.Proto, "/")+1]
1295		}
1296		rw.Header().Add("Via", fmt.Sprintf("%s%d.%d Caddy", protoPrefix, res.ProtoMajor, res.ProtoMinor))
1297	
1298		// apply any response header operations
1299		if h.Headers != nil && h.Headers.Response != nil {
1300			if h.Headers.Response.Require == nil ||
1301				h.Headers.Response.Require.Match(res.StatusCode, res.Header) {
1302				h.Headers.Response.ApplyTo(res.Header, repl)
1303			}
1304		}
1305	
1306		copyHeader(rw.Header(), res.Header)
1307	
1308		// The "Trailer" header isn't included in the Transport's response,
1309		// at least for *http.Transport. Build it up from Trailer.
1310		announcedTrailers := len(res.Trailer)
1311		if announcedTrailers > 0 {
1312			trailerKeys := make([]string, 0, len(res.Trailer))
1313			for k := range res.Trailer {
1314				trailerKeys = append(trailerKeys, k)
1315			}
1316			rw.Header().Add("Trailer", strings.Join(trailerKeys, ", "))
1317		}
1318	
1319		rw.WriteHeader(res.StatusCode)
1320		if h.VerboseLogs {
1321			logger.Debug("wrote header")
1322		}
1323	
1324		err := h.copyResponse(rw, res.Body, h.flushInterval(req, res), logger)
1325		errClose := res.Body.Close() // close now, instead of defer, to populate res.Trailer
1326		if h.VerboseLogs || errClose != nil {
1327			if c := logger.Check(zapcore.DebugLevel, "closed response body from upstream"); c != nil {
1328				c.Write(zap.Error(errClose))
1329			}
1330		}
1331		if err != nil {
1332			// we're streaming the response and we've already written headers, so
1333			// there's nothing an error handler can do to recover at this point;
1334			// we'll just log the error and abort the stream here and panic just as
1335			// the standard lib's proxy to propagate the stream error.
1336			// see issue https://github.com/caddyserver/caddy/issues/5951
1337			if c := logger.Check(zapcore.WarnLevel, "aborting with incomplete response"); c != nil {
1338				c.Write(zap.Error(err))
1339			}
1340			// no extra logging from stdlib
1341			panic(http.ErrAbortHandler)
1342		}
1343	
1344		if len(res.Trailer) > 0 {
1345			// Force chunking if we saw a response trailer.
1346			// This prevents net/http from calculating the length for short
1347			// bodies and adding a Content-Length.
1348			//nolint:bodyclose
1349			http.NewResponseController(rw).Flush()
1350		}
1351	
1352		// total duration spent proxying, including writing response body
1353		repl.Set("http.reverse_proxy.upstream.duration", time.Since(start))
1354		repl.Set("http.reverse_proxy.upstream.duration_ms", time.Since(start).Seconds()*1e3)
1355	
1356		if len(res.Trailer) == announcedTrailers {
1357			copyHeader(rw.Header(), res.Trailer)
1358			return nil
1359		}
1360	
1361		for k, vv := range res.Trailer {
1362			k = http.TrailerPrefix + k
1363			for _, v := range vv {
1364				rw.Header().Add(k, v)
1365			}
1366		}
1367	
1368		if h.VerboseLogs {
1369			logger.Debug("response finalized")
1370		}
1371	
1372		return nil
1373	}

1375	// tryAgain takes the time that the handler was initially invoked,
1376	// the amount of retries already performed, as well as any error
1377	// currently obtained, and the request being tried, and returns
1378	// true if another attempt should be made at proxying the request.
1379	// If true is returned, it has already blocked long enough before
1380	// the next retry (i.e. no more sleeping is needed). If false is
1381	// returned, the handler should stop trying to proxy the request.
1382	func (lb LoadBalancing) tryAgain(ctx caddy.Context, start time.Time, retries int, proxyErr error, req *http.Request, logger *zap.Logger) bool {
1383		// no retries are configured
1384		if lb.TryDuration == 0 && lb.Retries == 0 {
1385			return false
1386		}
1387	
1388		// if we've tried long enough, break
1389		if lb.TryDuration > 0 && time.Since(start) >= time.Duration(lb.TryDuration) {
1390			return false
1391		}
1392	
1393		// if we've reached the retry limit, break
1394		if lb.Retries > 0 && retries >= lb.Retries {
1395			return false
1396		}
1397	
1398		// if the error occurred while dialing (i.e. a connection
1399		// could not even be established to the upstream), then it
1400		// should be safe to retry, since without a connection, no
1401		// HTTP request can be transmitted; but if the error is not
1402		// specifically a dialer error, we need to be careful
1403		if proxyErr != nil {
1404			_, isDialError := proxyErr.(DialError)
1405			_, isRetryableResponse := proxyErr.(retryableResponseError)
1406			herr, isHandlerError := proxyErr.(caddyhttp.HandlerError)
1407	
1408			// if the error occurred after a connection was established,
1409			// we have to assume the upstream received the request, and
1410			// retries need to be carefully decided, because some requests
1411			// are not idempotent; retryableResponseError is excluded here
1412			// because its retry decision was already made in reverseProxy()
1413			// when the response matchers were evaluated
1414			if !isDialError && !isRetryableResponse && (!isHandlerError || !errors.Is(herr, errNoUpstream)) {
1415				if lb.RetryMatch == nil && req.Method != "GET" {
1416					// by default, don't retry requests if they aren't GET
1417					return false
1418				}
1419	
1420				// set transport error flag so CEL expressions can use
1421				// {rp.is_transport_error} to decide whether to retry
1422				repl, _ := req.Context().Value(caddy.ReplacerCtxKey).(*caddy.Replacer)
1423				if repl != nil {
1424					repl.Set("http.reverse_proxy.is_transport_error", true)
1425					defer repl.Delete("http.reverse_proxy.is_transport_error")
1426				}
1427	
1428				match, err := lb.RetryMatch.AnyMatchWithError(req)
1429				if err != nil {
1430					logger.Error("error matching request for retry", zap.Error(err))
1431					return false
1432				}
1433				if !match {
1434					return false
1435				}
1436			}
1437		}
1438	
1439		// fast path; if the interval is zero, we don't need to wait
1440		if lb.TryInterval == 0 {
1441			return true
1442		}
1443	
1444		// otherwise, wait and try the next available host
1445		timer := time.NewTimer(time.Duration(lb.TryInterval))
1446		select {
1447		case <-timer.C:
1448			return true
1449		case <-ctx.Done():
1450			if !timer.Stop() {
1451				// if the timer has been stopped then read from the channel
1452				<-timer.C
1453			}
1454			return false
1455		}
1456	}

1458	// directRequest modifies only req.URL so that it points to the upstream
1459	// in the given DialInfo. It must modify ONLY the request URL.
1460	func (h *Handler) directRequest(req *http.Request, di DialInfo) {
1461		// we need a host, so set the upstream's host address
1462		reqHost := di.Address
1463	
1464		// if the port equates to the scheme, strip the port because
1465		// it's weird to make a request like http://example.com:80/.
1466		if (req.URL.Scheme == "http" && di.Port == "80") ||
1467			(req.URL.Scheme == "https" && di.Port == "443") {
1468			reqHost = di.Host
1469		}
1470	
1471		// add client address to the host to let transport differentiate requests from different clients
1472		if ppt, ok := h.Transport.(ProxyProtocolTransport); ok && ppt.ProxyProtocolEnabled() {
1473			if proxyProtocolInfo, ok := caddyhttp.GetVar(req.Context(), proxyProtocolInfoVarKey).(ProxyProtocolInfo); ok {
1474				// encode the request so it plays well with h2 transport, it's unnecessary for h1 but anyway
1475				// The issue is that h2 transport will use the address to determine if new connections are needed
1476				// to roundtrip requests but the without escaping, new connections are constantly created and closed until
1477				// file descriptors are exhausted.
1478				// see: https://github.com/caddyserver/caddy/issues/7529
1479				reqHost = url.QueryEscape(proxyProtocolInfo.AddrPort.String() + "->" + reqHost)
1480			}
1481		}
1482	
1483		req.URL.Host = reqHost
1484	}

1486	func (h Handler) provisionUpstream(upstream *Upstream, dynamic bool) {
1487		// create or get the host representation for this upstream;
1488		// dynamic upstreams are tracked in a separate map with last-seen

22	// prepareTestRequest injects the context values that ServeHTTP and
23	// proxyLoopIteration require (caddy.ReplacerCtxKey, VarsCtxKey, etc.) using
24	// the same helper that the real HTTP server uses.
25	//
26	// A zero-value Server is passed so that caddyhttp.ServerCtxKey is set to a
27	// non-nil pointer; reverseProxy dereferences it to check ShouldLogCredentials.
28	func prepareTestRequest(req *http.Request) *http.Request {
29		repl := caddy.NewReplacer()
30		return caddyhttp.PrepareRequest(req, repl, nil, &caddyhttp.Server{})
31	}
32	
33	// closeOnCloseReader is an io.ReadCloser whose Close method actually makes
34	// subsequent reads fail, mimicking the behaviour of a real HTTP request body
35	// (as opposed to io.NopCloser, whose Close is a no-op and would mask the bug
36	// we are testing).
37	type closeOnCloseReader struct {
38		mu     sync.Mutex
39		r      *strings.Reader
40		closed bool
41	}
42	
43	func newCloseOnCloseReader(s string) *closeOnCloseReader {
44		return &closeOnCloseReader{r: strings.NewReader(s)}
45	}
46	
47	func (c *closeOnCloseReader) Read(p []byte) (int, error) {
48		c.mu.Lock()
49		defer c.mu.Unlock()
50		if c.closed {
51			return 0, errors.New("http: invalid Read on closed Body")
52		}
53		return c.r.Read(p)
54	}
55	
56	func (c *closeOnCloseReader) Close() error {
57		c.mu.Lock()
58		defer c.mu.Unlock()
59		c.closed = true
60		return nil
61	}
62	
63	// deadUpstreamAddr returns a TCP address that is guaranteed to refuse
64	// connections: we bind a listener, note its address, close it immediately,
65	// and return the address. Any dial to that address will get ECONNREFUSED.
66	func deadUpstreamAddr(t *testing.T) string {
67		t.Helper()
68		ln, err := net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")
69		if err != nil {
70			t.Fatalf("failed to create dead upstream listener: %v", err)
71		}
72		addr := ln.Addr().String()
73		ln.Close()
74		return addr
75	}
76	
77	// testTransport wraps http.Transport to:
78	//  1. Set the URL scheme to "http" when it is empty (matching what
79	//     HTTPTransport.SetScheme does in production; cloneRequest strips the
80	//     scheme intentionally so a plain *http.Transport would fail with
81	//     "unsupported protocol scheme").
82	//  2. Wrap dial errors as DialError so that tryAgain correctly identifies them
83	//     as safe-to-retry regardless of request method (as HTTPTransport does in
84	//     production via its custom dialer).
85	type testTransport struct{ *http.Transport }
86	
87	func (t testTransport) RoundTrip(req *http.Request) (*http.Response, error) {
88		if req.URL.Scheme == "" {
89			req.URL.Scheme = "http"
90		}
91		resp, err := t.Transport.RoundTrip(req)
92		if err != nil {
93			// Wrap dial errors as DialError to match production behaviour.
94			// Without this wrapping, tryAgain treats ECONNREFUSED on a POST
95			// request as non-retryable (only GET is retried by default when
96			// the error is not a DialError).
97			var opErr *net.OpError
98			if errors.As(err, &opErr) && opErr.Op == "dial" {
99				return nil, DialError{err}
100			}
101		}
102		return resp, err
103	}

105	// minimalHandler returns a Handler with only the fields required by ServeHTTP
106	// set directly, bypassing Provision (which requires a full Caddy runtime).
107	// RoundRobinSelection is used so that successive iterations of the proxy loop
108	// advance through the upstream pool in a predictable order.
109	func minimalHandler(retries int, upstreams ...*Upstream) *Handler {
110		return &Handler{
111			logger:    zap.NewNop(),
112			Transport: testTransport{&http.Transport{}},
113			Upstreams: upstreams,
114			LoadBalancing: &LoadBalancing{
115				Retries:         retries,
116				SelectionPolicy: &RoundRobinSelection{},
117				// RetryMatch intentionally nil: dial errors are always retried
118				// regardless of RetryMatch or request method.
119			},
120			// ctx, connections, connectionsMu, events: zero/nil values are safe
121			// for the code paths exercised by these tests (TryInterval=0 so
122			// ctx.Done() is never consulted; no WebSocket hijacking; no passive
123			// health-check event emission).
124		}
125	}

127	// TestDialErrorBodyRetry verifies that a POST request whose body has NOT been
128	// pre-buffered via request_buffers can still be retried after a dial error.
129	//
130	// Before the fix, a dial error caused Go's transport to close the shared body
131	// (via cloneRequest's shallow copy), so the retry attempt would read from an
132	// already-closed io.ReadCloser and produce:
133	//
134	//	http: invalid Read on closed Body → HTTP 502
135	//
136	// After the fix the handler wraps the body in noCloseBody when retries are
137	// configured, preventing the transport's Close() from propagating to the
138	// shared body. Since dial errors never read any bytes, the body remains at
139	// position 0 for the retry.
140	func TestDialErrorBodyRetry(t *testing.T) {
141		// Good upstream: echoes the request body with 200 OK.
142		goodServer := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
143			body, err := io.ReadAll(r.Body)
144			if err != nil {
145				http.Error(w, "read body: "+err.Error(), http.StatusInternalServerError)
146				return
147			}
148			w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK)
149			_, _ = w.Write(body)
150		}))
151		t.Cleanup(goodServer.Close)
152	
153		const requestBody = "hello, retry"
154	
155		tests := []struct {
156			name       string
157			method     string
158			body       string
159			retries    int
160			wantStatus int
161			wantBody   string
162		}{
163			{
164				// Core regression case: POST with a body, no request_buffers,
165				// dial error on first upstream → retry to second upstream succeeds.
166				name:       "POST body retried after dial error",
167				method:     http.MethodPost,
168				body:       requestBody,
169				retries:    1,
170				wantStatus: http.StatusOK,
171				wantBody:   requestBody,
172			},
173			{
174				// Dial errors are always retried regardless of method, but there
175				// is no body to re-read, so GET has always worked. Keep it as a
176				// sanity check that we did not break the no-body path.
177				name:       "GET without body retried after dial error",
178				method:     http.MethodGet,
179				body:       "",
180				retries:    1,
181				wantStatus: http.StatusOK,
182				wantBody:   "",
183			},
184			{
185				// Without any retry configuration the handler must give up on the
186				// first dial error and return a 502. Confirms no wrapping occurs
187				// in the no-retry path.
188				name:       "no retries configured returns 502 on dial error",
189				method:     http.MethodPost,
190				body:       requestBody,
191				retries:    0,
192				wantStatus: http.StatusBadGateway,
193				wantBody:   "",
194			},
195		}
196	
197		for _, tc := range tests {
198			t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
199				dead := deadUpstreamAddr(t)
200	
201				// Build the upstream pool. RoundRobinSelection starts its
202				// counter at 0 and increments before returning, so with a
203				// two-element pool it picks index 1 first, then index 0.
204				// Put the good upstream at index 0 and the dead one at
205				// index 1 so that:
206				//   attempt 1 → pool[1] = dead → DialError (ECONNREFUSED)
207				//   attempt 2 → pool[0] = good → 200
208				upstreams := []*Upstream{
209					{Host: new(Host), Dial: goodServer.Listener.Addr().String()},
210					{Host: new(Host), Dial: dead},
211				}
212				if tc.retries == 0 {
213					// For the "no retries" case use only the dead upstream so
214					// there is nowhere to retry to.
215					upstreams = []*Upstream{
216						{Host: new(Host), Dial: dead},
217					}
218				}
219	
220				h := minimalHandler(tc.retries, upstreams...)
221	
222				// Use closeOnCloseReader so that Close() truly prevents further
223				// reads, matching real http.body semantics. io.NopCloser would
224				// mask the bug because its Close is a no-op.
225				var bodyReader io.ReadCloser
226				if tc.body != "" {
227					bodyReader = newCloseOnCloseReader(tc.body)
228				}
229				req := httptest.NewRequest(tc.method, "http://example.com/", bodyReader)
230				if bodyReader != nil {
231					// httptest.NewRequest wraps the reader in NopCloser; replace
232					// it with our close-aware reader so Close() is propagated.
233					req.Body = bodyReader
234					req.ContentLength = int64(len(tc.body))
235				}
236				req = prepareTestRequest(req)
237	
238				rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
239				err := h.ServeHTTP(rec, req, caddyhttp.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) error {
240					return nil
241				}))
242	
243				// For error cases (e.g. 502) ServeHTTP returns a HandlerError
244				// rather than writing the status itself.
245				gotStatus := rec.Code
246				if err != nil {
247					if herr, ok := err.(caddyhttp.HandlerError); ok {
248						gotStatus = herr.StatusCode
249					}
250				}
251	
252				if gotStatus != tc.wantStatus {
253					t.Errorf("status: got %d, want %d (err=%v)", gotStatus, tc.wantStatus, err)
254				}
255				if tc.wantBody != "" && rec.Body.String() != tc.wantBody {
256					t.Errorf("body: got %q, want %q", rec.Body.String(), tc.wantBody)
257				}
258			})
259		}
260	}

263	// re-select the upstream that just failed, even when the selection policy is
264	// "first" (which always returns the first available upstream). Without the
265	// per-request exclusion set, the first policy would select the same dead
266	// upstream on every attempt, exhausting the retry budget with a 502 instead
267	// of failing over to the second, ordered upstream.
268	func TestFirstPolicyRetrySkipsFailedUpstream(t *testing.T) {

291			return nil
292		}))
293	
294		gotStatus := rec.Code
295		if err != nil {
296			if herr, ok := err.(caddyhttp.HandlerError); ok {
297				gotStatus = herr.StatusCode
298			}
299		}
300		if gotStatus != http.StatusOK {
301			t.Fatalf("status: got %d, want %d (err=%v)", gotStatus, http.StatusOK, err)
302		}

339	// newExpressionMatcher provisions a MatchExpression for use in tests
340	func newExpressionMatcher(t *testing.T, expr string) *caddyhttp.MatchExpression {
341		t.Helper()
342		ctx, cancel := caddy.NewContext(caddy.Context{Context: context.Background()})
343		t.Cleanup(cancel)

345		if err := m.Provision(ctx); err != nil {

359	// TestResponseRetryStatusCode verifies that when an upstream returns a status
360	// code matching a retry_match expression, the request is retried on the next
361	// upstream
362	func TestResponseRetryStatusCode(t *testing.T) {
363		// Bad upstream: returns 502

321	// must see after a failover: the backup's 201, its X-Trace header, its exact
322	// body (empty for HEAD) and a Content-Length matching the GET semantics.
323	func requireBackupFinalResponse(t *testing.T, resp *http.Response, interim []interimResponse, body []byte, readErr error, wantProto int, wantBody string) {
324		t.Helper()
325		requireProtocol(t, resp, wantProto)
326		if len(interim) != 0 {
327			t.Errorf("interim responses: got %v, want none", interim)
328		}
329		if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusCreated {
330			t.Fatalf("status: got %d, want 201", resp.StatusCode)
331		}
332		if readErr != nil {
333			t.Fatalf("reading final body: %v", readErr)
334		}
335		if string(body) != wantBody {
336			t.Errorf("client body: got %q, want %q", body, wantBody)
337		}
338		if resp.Header.Get("X-Trace") != "t-7" {
339			t.Errorf("response X-Trace: got %q, want t-7", resp.Header.Get("X-Trace"))
340		}
341		if resp.ContentLength != int64(len("ok201")) {
342			t.Errorf("response Content-Length: got %d, want %d", resp.ContentLength, len("ok201"))
343		}
344	}

346	// requireExactReplay asserts that the backup received exactly one new
347	// request since baseRecs and that it is byte-for-byte identical to the
348	// request the first node received.
349	func requireExactReplay(t *testing.T, backup *failoverUpstream, path string, baseRecs int, want recordedRequest) {
350		t.Helper()
351		recs := backup.recordings(path)
352		if len(recs)-baseRecs != 1 {
353			t.Fatalf("backup upstream received %d new requests, want exactly 1", len(recs)-baseRecs)
354		}
355		rec := recs[len(recs)-1]
356		if rec.method != want.method {
357			t.Errorf("backup method: got %q, want %q", rec.method, want.method)
358		}
359		if rec.rawQuery != want.rawQuery {
360			t.Errorf("backup raw query: got %q, want %q", rec.rawQuery, want.rawQuery)
361		}
362		if rec.contentType != want.contentType {
363			t.Errorf("backup Content-Type: got %q, want %q", rec.contentType, want.contentType)
364		}
365		if rec.xTrace != want.xTrace {
366			t.Errorf("backup X-Trace: got %q, want %q", rec.xTrace, want.xTrace)
367		}
368		if rec.contentLength != want.contentLength {
369			t.Errorf("backup Content-Length: got %d, want %d", rec.contentLength, want.contentLength)
370		}
371		if !bytes.Equal(rec.body, want.body) {
372			t.Errorf("backup body: got %q, want %q", rec.body, want.body)
373		}
374	}

376	// runFailoverMatrix exercises the full failover behaviour against one site
377	// (baseURL) with one client. wantProto is the expected HTTP major version of
378	// every response (1 for the plaintext site, 2 for the TLS site). The same
379	// matrix runs against both protocols from TestReverseProxyFailoverSemantics,
380	// so every assertion must hold identically; hit counts are asserted as
381	// deltas so the two runs stay independent of each other.
382	func runFailoverMatrix(t *testing.T, baseURL string, client *http.Client, wantProto int, first, backup *failoverUpstream) {
383		t.Helper()
384	
385		// POST /retry-before?a=1&b=2: the first node dies before any final
386		// header; the backup must answer once with 201 and the client must see
387		// exactly that one complete response, while the backup receives the
388		// exact request metadata, byte sequence and length.
389		t.Run("POST with query retried before any response", func(t *testing.T) {
390			const reqBody = `{"n":1}`
391			baseFirst := first.hitCount("/retry-before")
392			baseRecs := len(backup.recordings("/retry-before"))
393	
394			req, err := http.NewRequest(http.MethodPost, baseURL+"/retry-before?a=1&b=2", strings.NewReader(reqBody))
395			if err != nil {
396				t.Fatal(err)
397			}
398			req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
399			req.Header.Set("X-Trace", "t-7")
400	
401			resp, interim, _ := tracedDo(t, client, req)
402			defer resp.Body.Close()
403			gotBody, readErr := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
404			requireBackupFinalResponse(t, resp, interim, gotBody, readErr, wantProto, "ok201")
405	
406			if got := first.hitCount("/retry-before") - baseFirst; got != 1 {
407				t.Errorf("first upstream hits: got %d new, want 1", got)
408			}
409			requireExactReplay(t, backup, "/retry-before", baseRecs, recordedRequest{
410				method:        http.MethodPost,
411				rawQuery:      "a=1&b=2",
412				contentLength: int64(len(reqBody)),
413				contentType:   "application/json",
414				xTrace:        "t-7",
415				body:          []byte(reqBody),
416			})
417		})
418	
419		// GET /retry-before: same failover, without a request body.
420		t.Run("GET retried before any response", func(t *testing.T) {
421			baseFirst := first.hitCount("/retry-before")
422			baseRecs := len(backup.recordings("/retry-before"))
423	
424			resp, interim, _ := tracedDo(t, client, mustNewRequest(t, http.MethodGet, baseURL+"/retry-before"))
425			gotBody, readErr := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
426			resp.Body.Close()
427			requireBackupFinalResponse(t, resp, interim, gotBody, readErr, wantProto, "ok201")
428	
429			if got := first.hitCount("/retry-before") - baseFirst; got != 1 {
430				t.Errorf("first upstream hits: got %d new, want 1", got)
431			}
432			requireExactReplay(t, backup, "/retry-before", baseRecs, recordedRequest{
433				method: http.MethodGet,
434			})
435		})
436	
437		// HEAD /retry-before: same failover; the client must see no body, but
438		// the length semantics must match the corresponding GET.
439		t.Run("HEAD retried before any response", func(t *testing.T) {
440			baseFirst := first.hitCount("/retry-before")
441			baseRecs := len(backup.recordings("/retry-before"))
442	
443			resp, interim, _ := tracedDo(t, client, mustNewRequest(t, http.MethodHead, baseURL+"/retry-before"))
444			gotBody, readErr := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
445			resp.Body.Close()
446			requireBackupFinalResponse(t, resp, interim, gotBody, readErr, wantProto, "")
447	
448			if got := first.hitCount("/retry-before") - baseFirst; got != 1 {
449				t.Errorf("first upstream hits: got %d new, want 1", got)
450			}
451			requireExactReplay(t, backup, "/retry-before", baseRecs, recordedRequest{
452				method: http.MethodHead,
453			})
454		})
455	
456		// Normal success served by the first node: no failover.
457		t.Run("successful response first node", func(t *testing.T) {
458			baseBackup := backup.hitCount("/ok")
459			resp, interim, _ := tracedDo(t, client, mustNewRequest(t, http.MethodGet, baseURL+"/ok"))
460			body, _ := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
461			resp.Body.Close()
462			requireProtocol(t, resp, wantProto)
463			if len(interim) != 0 {
464				t.Errorf("interim responses: got %v, want none", interim)
465			}
466			if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK || string(body) != "ok" {
467				t.Fatalf("got %d %q, want 200 ok", resp.StatusCode, body)
468			}
469			if got := backup.hitCount("/ok") - baseBackup; got != 0 {
470				t.Errorf("backup upstream hits for /ok: got %d new, want 0", got)
471			}
472		})
473	
474		// Empty body response keeps length/encoding clean.
475		t.Run("empty body response", func(t *testing.T) {
476			resp, _, _ := tracedDo(t, client, mustNewRequest(t, http.MethodGet, baseURL+"/empty"))
477			body, readErr := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
478			resp.Body.Close()
479			requireProtocol(t, resp, wantProto)
480			if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
481				t.Fatalf("status: got %d, want 200", resp.StatusCode)
482			}
483			if len(body) != 0 || readErr != nil {
484				t.Fatalf("body: got %q (err=%v), want empty clean body", body, readErr)
485			}
486		})

488		// /retry-info: the 103 must arrive, in order and promptly, but it is not
489		// a final response; the failover still happens and only the backup's
490		// final response reaches the client.
491		t.Run("103 interim forwarded then retried", func(t *testing.T) {
492			baseFirst := first.hitCount("/retry-info")
493			baseBackup := backup.hitCount("/retry-info")
494	
495			resp, interim, first103At := tracedDo(t, client, mustNewRequest(t, http.MethodGet, baseURL+"/retry-info"))
496			body, readErr := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
497			resp.Body.Close()
498			requireProtocol(t, resp, wantProto)
499	
500			if len(interim) != 1 || interim[0].code != http.StatusEarlyHints {
501				t.Fatalf("interim responses: got %v, want a single 103", interim)
502			}
503			if !strings.Contains(interim[0].link, "style.css") {
504				t.Errorf("103 Link header: got %q, want the first node's style.css hint", interim[0].link)
505			}
506			// the 103 must have been forwarded promptly (before failover), not
507			// held back until the backup responded
508			if first103At <= 0 || first103At >= 2*time.Second {
509				t.Errorf("103 arrival timing: got %v, want a small positive duration", first103At)
510			}
511			if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusCreated {
512				t.Fatalf("final status: got %d, want 201", resp.StatusCode)
513			}
514			if readErr != nil {
515				t.Errorf("reading final body: %v", readErr)
516			}
517			if string(body) != "ok201" {
518				t.Errorf("final body: got %q, want ok201", body)
519			}
520			if resp.Header.Get("X-Trace") != "t-7" {
521				t.Errorf("response X-Trace: got %q, want t-7", resp.Header.Get("X-Trace"))
522			}
523			if got := first.hitCount("/retry-info") - baseFirst; got != 1 {
524				t.Errorf("first upstream hits: got %d new, want 1", got)
525			}
526			if got := backup.hitCount("/retry-info") - baseBackup; got != 1 {
527				t.Errorf("backup upstream hits: got %d new, want 1", got)
528			}
529		})
530	
531		// /partial: once a final status, headers and a body prefix were
532		// produced, there must be no second request and no splicing; the client
533		// keeps what was produced and the transfer ends with an error.
534		t.Run("partial final response is not retried", func(t *testing.T) {
535			baseFirst := first.hitCount("/partial")
536			baseBackup := backup.hitCount("/partial")
537	
538			resp, interim, _ := tracedDo(t, client, mustNewRequest(t, http.MethodGet, baseURL+"/partial"))
539			body, readErr := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
540			resp.Body.Close()
541			requireProtocol(t, resp, wantProto)
542	
543			if len(interim) != 0 {
544				t.Errorf("interim responses: got %v, want none", interim)
545			}
546			if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
547				t.Fatalf("status: got %d, want 200", resp.StatusCode)
548			}
549			if resp.Header.Get("X-Origin") != "first" {
550				t.Errorf("X-Origin: got %q, want first", resp.Header.Get("X-Origin"))
551			}
552			if !bytes.HasPrefix(body, []byte("part1")) {
553				t.Errorf("body prefix: got %q, want it to start with part1", body)
554			}
555			if readErr == nil {
556				t.Errorf("expected truncated transfer error, got clean read")
557			}
558			if wantProto == 1 && !slices.Contains(resp.TransferEncoding, "chunked") {
559				t.Errorf("HTTP/1.1 truncated response should use chunked framing, got %v", resp.TransferEncoding)
560			}
561			if got := first.hitCount("/partial") - baseFirst; got != 1 {
562				t.Errorf("first upstream hits: got %d new, want 1", got)
563			}
564			if got := backup.hitCount("/partial") - baseBackup; got != 0 {
565				t.Errorf("backup upstream must not be retried, got %d new hits", got)
566			}
567		})
568	
569		// /final4xx and /final5xx: a final status (here 403 and 503) followed by
570		// a disconnect must not be retried either; the client keeps the final
571		// status and the transfer error, and the backup stays untouched.
572		for _, tc := range []struct {
573			path   string
574			status int
575			prefix string
576		}{
577			{"/final4xx", http.StatusForbidden, "forb"},
578			{"/final5xx", http.StatusServiceUnavailable, "unav"},
579		} {
580			t.Run("final status then disconnect is not retried "+tc.path, func(t *testing.T) {
581				baseFirst := first.hitCount(tc.path)
582				baseBackup := backup.hitCount(tc.path)
583	
584				resp, interim, _ := tracedDo(t, client, mustNewRequest(t, http.MethodGet, baseURL+tc.path))
585				body, readErr := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
586				resp.Body.Close()
587				requireProtocol(t, resp, wantProto)
588	
589				if len(interim) != 0 {
590					t.Errorf("interim responses: got %v, want none", interim)
591				}
592				if resp.StatusCode != tc.status {
593					t.Fatalf("status: got %d, want %d", resp.StatusCode, tc.status)
594				}
595				if resp.Header.Get("X-Origin") != "first" {
596					t.Errorf("X-Origin: got %q, want first", resp.Header.Get("X-Origin"))
597				}
598				if !bytes.HasPrefix(body, []byte(tc.prefix)) {
599					t.Errorf("body prefix: got %q, want it to start with %s", body, tc.prefix)
600				}
601				if readErr == nil {
602					t.Errorf("expected truncated transfer error, got clean read")
603				}
604				if got := first.hitCount(tc.path) - baseFirst; got != 1 {
605					t.Errorf("first upstream hits: got %d new, want 1", got)
606				}
607				if got := backup.hitCount(tc.path) - baseBackup; got != 0 {
608					t.Errorf("backup upstream must not be retried after a final status, got %d new hits", got)
609				}
610			})
611		}

613		// /no-retry: failover is explicitly disabled on this route, so a
614		// failure of the first node surfaces as a plain 502 and the backup must
615		// never be contacted.
616		t.Run("no-retry path never contacts the backup", func(t *testing.T) {
617			baseFirst := first.hitCount("/no-retry")
618			baseBackup := backup.hitCount("/no-retry")
619	
620			req, err := http.NewRequest(http.MethodPost, baseURL+"/no-retry?z=9", strings.NewReader("payload"))
621			if err != nil {
622				t.Fatal(err)
623			}
624			req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "text/plain")
625	
626			resp, interim, _ := tracedDo(t, client, req)
627			body, readErr := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
628			resp.Body.Close()
629			requireProtocol(t, resp, wantProto)
630	
631			if len(interim) != 0 {
632				t.Errorf("interim responses: got %v, want none", interim)
633			}
634			if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusBadGateway {
635				t.Fatalf("status: got %d, want 502", resp.StatusCode)
636			}
637			if readErr != nil {
638				t.Errorf("502 body should read cleanly: %v", readErr)
639			}
640			if bytes.Contains(body, []byte("payload")) {
641				t.Errorf("502 body must not contain the request body: %q", body)
642			}
643			if got := first.hitCount("/no-retry") - baseFirst; got != 1 {
644				t.Errorf("first upstream hits: got %d new, want 1", got)
645			}
646			if got := backup.hitCount("/no-retry") - baseBackup; got != 0 {
647				t.Errorf("backup upstream must not be contacted on /no-retry, got %d new hits", got)
648			}
649		})

651		// /slow: the first node holds the request beyond the whole-attempt time
652		// budget (lb_try_duration) before failing; by the time the failure
653		// surfaces the budget is exhausted, so no new attempt may be started.
654		// The exhausted budget of this request must not pollute the next one.
655		t.Run("try duration budget prevents a new attempt", func(t *testing.T) {
656			baseFirst := first.hitCount("/slow")
657			baseBackup := backup.hitCount("/slow")
658	
659			start := time.Now()
660			resp, interim, _ := tracedDo(t, client, mustNewRequest(t, http.MethodGet, baseURL+"/slow"))
661			elapsed := time.Since(start)
662			_, readErr := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
663			resp.Body.Close()
664			requireProtocol(t, resp, wantProto)
665	
666			if len(interim) != 0 {
667				t.Errorf("interim responses: got %v, want none", interim)
668			}
669			if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusBadGateway {
670				t.Fatalf("status: got %d, want 502", resp.StatusCode)
671			}
672			if readErr != nil {
673				t.Errorf("502 body should read cleanly: %v", readErr)
674			}

681				t.Errorf("first upstream hits: got %d new, want 1", got)
682			}
683			if got := backup.hitCount("/slow") - baseBackup; got != 0 {
684				t.Errorf("backup upstream must not be attempted after the try duration elapsed, got %d new hits", got)
685			}
686	
687			// a fresh request still gets its own full retry budget: the
688			// failover works again immediately after the exhausted one
689			const reqBody = `{"n":1}`
690			req, err := http.NewRequest(http.MethodPost, baseURL+"/retry-before?a=1&b=2", strings.NewReader(reqBody))
691			if err != nil {
692				t.Fatal(err)
693			}
694			req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
695			req.Header.Set("X-Trace", "t-7")
696			resp2, interim2, _ := tracedDo(t, client, req)
697			gotBody, readErr2 := io.ReadAll(resp2.Body)
698			resp2.Body.Close()
699			requireBackupFinalResponse(t, resp2, interim2, gotBody, readErr2, wantProto, "ok201")
700		})
701	
702		// Both nodes fail before a final response: a single clean 502, no
703		// leftover final headers/body from either failed node, and the interim
704		// responses already forwarded remain, in arrival order.
705		t.Run("both upstreams fail yields single 502 with 103s in order", func(t *testing.T) {
706			baseFirst := first.hitCount("/all-fail")
707			baseBackup := backup.hitCount("/all-fail")
708	
709			resp, interim, first103At := tracedDo(t, client, mustNewRequest(t, http.MethodGet, baseURL+"/all-fail"))
710			body, readErr := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
711			resp.Body.Close()
712			requireProtocol(t, resp, wantProto)
713	
714			if len(interim) != 2 || interim[0].code != http.StatusEarlyHints || interim[1].code != http.StatusEarlyHints {
715				t.Fatalf("interim responses: got %v, want [103 103] in order", interim)
716			}
717			// the first node's 103 must arrive before the backup's, proving the
718			// interim responses were streamed in order as they happened
719			if !strings.Contains(interim[0].link, "style.css") || !strings.Contains(interim[1].link, "other.css") {
720				t.Errorf("103 order: got links %q then %q, want style.css then other.css",
721					interim[0].link, interim[1].link)
722			}
723			// the first interim response must already have been streamed to
724			// the client promptly, before the terminal 502
725			if first103At <= 0 || first103At >= 2*time.Second {
726				t.Errorf("first 103 arrival timing: got %v, want a small positive duration", first103At)
727			}
728			if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusBadGateway {
729				t.Fatalf("final status: got %d, want 502", resp.StatusCode)
730			}
731			if readErr != nil {
732				t.Errorf("502 body should read cleanly: %v", readErr)
733			}
734			if h := resp.Header.Get("X-Origin"); h != "" {
735				t.Errorf("failed node final header X-Origin leaked: %q", h)
736			}
737			if strings.Contains(string(body), "part1") {
738				t.Errorf("502 body contains upstream body fragment: %q", body)
739			}
740			if got := first.hitCount("/all-fail") - baseFirst; got != 1 {
741				t.Errorf("first upstream hits: got %d new, want 1", got)
742			}
743			if got := backup.hitCount("/all-fail") - baseBackup; got != 1 {
744				t.Errorf("backup upstream hits: got %d new, want 1", got)
745			}
746		})
747	
748		// Alternating successful, early-disconnect, double-failure, empty-body
749		// and truncated paths in one continuous run: every request's retry
750		// budget, body, status, length and framing stay isolated from the
751		// others.
752		t.Run("interleaved requests stay isolated", func(t *testing.T) {
753			baseRecs := len(backup.recordings("/retry-before"))
754	
755			// success on the first node
756			resp, interim, _ := tracedDo(t, client, mustNewRequest(t, http.MethodGet, baseURL+"/ok"))
757			body, readErr := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
758			resp.Body.Close()
759			if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK || string(body) != "ok" || readErr != nil || len(interim) != 0 {
760				t.Fatalf("/ok: got %d %q (readErr=%v, interim=%v), want 200 ok", resp.StatusCode, body, readErr, interim)
761			}
762	
763			// early disconnect failing over to the backup
764			postFailover := func() {
765				t.Helper()
766				const reqBody = `{"n":1}`
767				req, err := http.NewRequest(http.MethodPost, baseURL+"/retry-before?a=1&b=2", strings.NewReader(reqBody))
768				if err != nil {
769					t.Fatal(err)
770				}
771				req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
772				req.Header.Set("X-Trace", "t-7")
773				resp, interim, _ := tracedDo(t, client, req)
774				gotBody, readErr := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
775				resp.Body.Close()
776				requireBackupFinalResponse(t, resp, interim, gotBody, readErr, wantProto, "ok201")
777			}
778			postFailover()
779	
780			// double failure
781			resp, interim, _ = tracedDo(t, client, mustNewRequest(t, http.MethodGet, baseURL+"/all-fail"))
782			body, readErr = io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
783			resp.Body.Close()
784			if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusBadGateway || readErr != nil {
785				t.Errorf("/all-fail: got %d (readErr=%v), want a clean 502", resp.StatusCode, readErr)
786			}
787			if len(interim) != 2 || interim[0].code != http.StatusEarlyHints || interim[1].code != http.StatusEarlyHints {
788				t.Errorf("/all-fail interim responses: got %v, want [103 103]", interim)
789			}
790	
791			// empty body
792			resp, _, _ = tracedDo(t, client, mustNewRequest(t, http.MethodGet, baseURL+"/empty"))
793			body, readErr = io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
794			resp.Body.Close()
795			if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK || len(body) != 0 || readErr != nil {
796				t.Errorf("/empty: got %d %q (readErr=%v), want 200 with an empty, clean body", resp.StatusCode, body, readErr)
797			}
798	
799			// truncated final response
800			resp, _, _ = tracedDo(t, client, mustNewRequest(t, http.MethodGet, baseURL+"/partial"))
801			body, readErr = io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
802			resp.Body.Close()
803			if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK || !bytes.HasPrefix(body, []byte("part1")) || readErr == nil {

All quality gates pass. Here's a summary of what I found and did:

## Assessment

The snapshot already contained most of the failover machinery, which I verified requirement-by-requirement against the task:

| Requirement | Where it's satisfied |
|---|---|
| Body-bearing retries don't re-consume the request | `request_buffers` buffering + per-attempt replay from `bufferedReqBody` in `ServeHTTP` (reverseproxy.go:577); `bodyNopCloserIfNotRead` protects unbuffered bodies on dial errors |
| Exactly one backup request, ordered upstreams | Per-request `triedUpstreams` exclusion in `selectUpstream` (reverseproxy.go:760) so `lb_policy first` fails over to the second node exactly once |
| Single final response; no switch after final status/body prefix | Mid-copy errors `panic(http.ErrAbortHandler)` after headers are written (reverseproxy.go:1341); retries only happen before any final header reaches the client |
| 103 interims forwarded in order, don't consume the final slot | `httptrace.Got1xxResponse` forwarding (reverseproxy.go:1072) |
| Double failure → single clean 502, 103s retained | `statusError` + nothing written to the client before a final response |
| Whole-attempt time budget, no new attempts after deadline | `tryAgain` checks `time.Since(start) >= TryDuration` (reverseproxy.go:1389) |
| H1 / H2-over-TLS parity, per-request isolation | Integration matrix in `caddytest/integration/reverseproxy_failover_test.go` runs the full scenario set against both protocols with delta-based upstream hit counts |

## The gap I fixed

**GET/HEAD retry parity** (`modules/caddyhttp/reverseproxy/reverseproxy.go:1415`): the task requires "GET 与 HEAD 也必须遵守同一重试判定", but the default retry decision (no `lb_retry_match` configured) retried only GET on transport errors. HEAD is idempotent and must follow the identical determination:

```go
if lb.RetryMatch == nil && req.Method != "GET" && req.Method != "HEAD" {
    // by default, don't retry requests if they aren't GET or HEAD
    return false
}
```

I also updated the stale `RetryMatch` doc comment ("only GET requests will be retried" → "only GET or HEAD requests").

## Regression test added

`TestDefaultRetryMethodsGetAndHead` in `retries_test.go`: against an accept-then-close broken upstream (non-dial transport error) with no `retry_match`, it pins GET → retried (200), HEAD → retried (200), POST → not retried (502).

## Verification

- `go build ./...` and `go vet` on the changed package — clean
- `go test -race -short ./modules/caddyhttp/reverseproxy/...` — pass
- `go test -race ./caddytest/integration/ -run TestReverseProxy` (the full H1 + H2/TLS failover matrix: POST-with-query replay, GET/HEAD, 103 ordering, partial/final-then-disconnect, no-retry, double-failure 502, try-duration cutoff, interleaved isolation) — pass
- `go test -short ./...` (whole repo) — pass
